title: Sprint footprint
description: The machine-readable declaration of what a sprint touches, so two active sprints can be checked for disjointness instead of trusted. Emitted as a fenced `json` block titled `Sprint Footprint` in the sprint file. The four implementation axes come from wave-executable-seams' four-condition disjointness rule; `closeArtifacts` and `baseRevision` were added after the first real concurrent dispatch showed the four axes call two sprints disjoint that demonstrably collide.

sprint.description: The sprint id token, matching SPRINT.<ID> in the filename.

capabilities.description: Disjointness condition 1. Capability names this sprint writes into.

fileGlobs.description: Disjointness condition 1. Globs this sprint may modify. Anything outside is out of footprint.

persistentResources.description: Disjointness condition 2. Tables, topics, queues, caches, migrations.

configKeysWritten.description: Disjointness condition 3. Configuration keys this sprint writes.

dependsOnContracts.description: Disjointness condition 4. Frozen `<name>@vN` seam contracts this sprint builds against, never the producer's in-flight internals.

closeArtifacts.description: Files this sprint must write at close but not during implementation — CHANGELOG, product dashboard, wave README, capability records. NOT part of the four-condition rule, and the reason it was insufficient: two sprints can be disjoint on all four implementation axes for their entire lifetime and still collide the moment they land. Overlap here does not forbid concurrency; it requires close to be reconciled centrally rather than raced.

baseRevision.description: The commit the sprint's engineering current-state snapshot was frozen against. A concurrent dispatch that cuts a worktree from the wrong base builds against a stale tree while every contract hash still matches, so contract freshness alone cannot catch it.

crossFootprintCriteria.description: Acceptance criteria that can be written by this sprint but only verified against a file outside its fileGlobs. Each needs a mechanical binding (a required phrase, a generated block) or it matches by construction today and silently un-closes tomorrow.
